The multi-material coating stack consists of 7 bilayers of SiO2/Ta2O5 in the outer layers and 5 bilayers of aSi/SiO2 in the inner layers.
The total thickness of the multi-material coating is 5.701 μm, reduced by 34% compared to the 8.684 μm thickness of the standard SiO2/Ta2O5 coating.
The measured optical absorption of the SiO2/Ta2O5 coating at 1550 nm was (1.7 ± 0.3) ppm.
The measured optical absorption of the aSi/SiO2 coating at 1550 nm and 42° angle of incidence was (1035 ± 42) ppm for s-polarization and (1428 ± 97) ppm for p-polarization.
The authors conclude that a total optical absorption of as low as (5.3 ± 0.4) ppm can be achieved for the multi-material coating stack.
Cryogenic operation temperatures of 120 K, 20 K, and even 10 K are planned for future gravitational wave detectors to reduce thermal noise.
Amorphous silicon (aSi) has a significantly higher refractive index (n = 3.5) than Ta2O5 (n = 2.2) at 1550 nm.
The mechanical loss of aSi is at least a factor of 10 lower than that of Ta2O5 at low temperatures.
The multi-material coating design is expected to reduce Brownian thermal noise by 25% compared to the standard SiO2/Ta2O5 coating.
At room temperature, the multi-material coating has slightly higher loss than the SiO2/Ta2O5 coating, but at lower temperatures the loss of the multi-material coating becomes lower.
The reduction in Brownian thermal noise for the multi-material coating is 15-20% compared to the SiO2/Ta2O5 coating at low temperatures.
The multi-material coating design uses the low-absorbing Ta2O5 in the outer layers to reflect most of the incident light, while the higher-index aSi is used only in the inner layers.
The multi-material coating stack has 26 single layers in total, reduced from 38 layers in the standard SiO2/Ta2O5 coating.
The authors measured the optical absorption of a SiO2/Ta2O5 coating stack at 1550 nm for the first time, reporting a value of (1.7 ± 0.3) ppm.
The authors also discuss new aspects of the optical absorption measurements for an aSi/SiO2 coating stack previously published in [11].
